To create ease for depositors in withdrawing their deposits from banks, the State Bank in August 2002 instructed all scheduled banks that they start the series of Automated Teller Machines (Automated Teller Machines: ATM) and the ATM Switch Network (ATM Switch Network).

A subsidiary institution of the State Bank was established in February 2002 whose name is: “National Institute of Banking and Finance” (National Institute of Banking and Finance: NIBAF). Ninety per cent of its shares are the property of the State Bank of Pakistan and ten per cent of the National Bank of Pakistan. This institution performs the following functions:

i. training of the officers of the State Bank of Pakistan;

Under this scheme a loan given up to three lakh rupees is called a small loan. The loan given to such industrial units and cottage industries the value of whose fixed assets (Fixed Assests), i.e. except land and buildings, is two crore rupees, is also called a small loan.

Reform of the banking system (Reform of Banking System)

For the reform of the banking system it is necessary that:

(i) monetary policy be put into practice through market-based instruments (Market-based instruments);

(ii) while giving loans, full care be taken of their supervision and protection;

(iii) for complete supervision of banks and creating regularity in their business, more authority be given to the State Bank;

(iv) the practice of giving loans on political grounds be controlled.

(continued from p.203) … board has these responsibilities: macro-economic stability (Macro-economic Stability), review of the expenditure occurring in connection with government borrowing and lending, and the correct use of credit loans etc.

11. Facility of automatic machines

To create ease for depositors in withdrawing their deposits from banks, the State Bank in August 2002 instructed all scheduled banks that they start the series of Automated Teller Machines (Automated Teller Machines: ATM) and the ATM Switch Network (ATM Switch Network).

12. Establishment of Islamic banking

To promote Islamic banking, the State Bank on 1 January 2003 instructed ordinary banks that the banks in the private sector which want to establish scheduled Islamic commercial banks should apply for this purpose to the director of the “Banking Policy Department” of the State Bank.

13. National institute of banking and finance

A subsidiary institution of the State Bank was established in February 2002 whose name is: “National Institute of Banking and Finance” (National Institute of Banking and Finance: NIBAF). Ninety per cent of its shares are the property of the State Bank of Pakistan and ten per cent of the National Bank of Pakistan. This institution performs the following functions:

i. training of the officers of the State Bank of Pakistan;

ii. devising different forms of institutional training;

iii. preparation of foundation courses and international courses.

This institution has a close link with the human resources department (training department) of the State Bank. Its headquarters is in Islamabad. This institution makes different training programmes and prepares booklets and journals in this connection. Further, it carries out research related to economics, banking and finance and arranges experts for giving training.

14. Scheme of small loans (Micro Credit Scheme)

Under this scheme a loan given up to three lakh rupees is called a small loan. The loan given to such industrial units and cottage industries the value of whose fixed assets (Fixed Assests), i.e. except land and buildings, is two crore rupees, is also called a small loan.

Reform of the banking system (Reform of Banking System)

For the reform of the banking system it is necessary that:

(i) monetary policy be put into practice through market-based instruments (Market-based instruments);

(ii) while giving loans, full care be taken of their supervision and protection;

(iii) for complete supervision of banks and creating regularity in their business, more authority be given to the State Bank;

(iv) the practice of giving loans on political grounds be controlled.

☆ طلبی قرضہ کے ادارے: ملک کے تجارتی بینک تھوڑی مدت کے لئے قرضہ دیتے ہیں اور سٹاک ایکس چینج (یعنی ایسے ادارے جو حصص، کفالتیں اور بانڈز خرید و فروخت کرتے ہیں) میں کام کرنے والے ہنڈیوں اور حصص کی خرید و فروخت کرنے والے طلبی قرضہ لیتے ہیں۔

☆ طویل مدت قرضہ کے ادارے: طویل مدت کے لئے عوام اپنی بچتوں کی شکل میں قرضہ دیتے ہیں، یعنی اپنا سرمایہ کفالتوں، مشترکہ سرمایہ کی کمپنیوں کے حصص اور بانڈوں میں لگا دیتے ہیں۔ خصوصی قرضہ کے ادارے یہ ہیں: پاکستان صنعتی ترقیاتی بینک، پاکستان صنعتی قرضہ و سرمایہ کاری کارپوریشن، تعمیر مکانات کی مالی کارپوریشن، پاکستان زرعی ترقیاتی بینک اور امدادِ باہمی کے بینک وغیرہ۔

New measures

Recently, for the reform and development of banks, the State Bank has established an inspection framework (Supervisory Framework) by the name of CAMELS (Camels), which keeps in view the analysis of six indicators (Indicators) that show the financial condition of banks and financial institutions. These indicators are entered below:

(1) whether the capital of the bank (i.e. C — Capital) is sufficient or not;

(2) whether the quality of the assets of the bank (i.e. A — Assets) is satisfactory or not;

(3) whether the management (i.e. M — Management) is strong and stable or not;

(4) whether income (i.e. E — Earning) and profitability are satisfactory or not;

(5) to what extent liquidity (i.e. L — Liquidity) is present;

(6) how the sensitivity (i.e. S — Sensitivity) is in facing the dangers and risks coming up in the market. Thus the review of the performance of all banking and non-banking financial institutions is made on the basis of “CAMELS”.

Money market (Money Market)

By the money market are meant such financial institutions (Financial Institutions) as do the work of buying and selling the following commercial papers: commercial bills (Treasury Bills), guarantees, bonds and the shares (Shares) of joint-stock companies. Thus these institutions are included in the money market:

☆ institutions buying and discounting bills (Discount Houses);

☆ institutions bringing together the buyers and discounters of bills (Bill Brokers);

☆ institutions buying and selling guarantees, bonds and shares;

☆ loan-giving institutions, i.e. banks.

All these institutions compete with one another in connection with giving and taking loans, and in this way the money market becomes strong and stable. The money market of Pakistan consists of the following:

☆ State Bank of Pakistan: this is the central bank of the country and controls the banking and monetary system of the country.

☆ Institutions of call (demand) loans: the commercial banks of the country give loans for a short period, and the people dealing in bills and shares working in the stock exchange (i.e. such institutions as buy and sell shares, guarantees and bonds) take call loans.

☆ Institutions of long-term loans: for the long term the public gives loans in the form of its savings, i.e. puts its capital in guarantees, shares of joint-stock companies and bonds. The special credit institutions are these: Pakistan Industrial Development Bank, Pakistan Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation, House Building Finance Corporation, Pakistan Zarai Taraqiati Bank and co-operative banks etc.

حال ہی میں بینکوں کی اصلاح و ترقی کے لئے سٹیٹ بینک نے ایک معائناتی قالب (Supervisory Framework) کیملز (Camels) کے نام سے قائم کیا ہے، جو بینکوں اور مالی اداروں کی مالی حالت کو ظاہر کرنے والے چھے مظاہر (Indicators) کے تجزیے کو پیشِ نظر رکھتا ہے۔ یہ مظاہر درج ذیل ہیں:
